# Game compatibility

<!-- Generated from patches/<Game>/game.ini by tools/dev/gen-compatibility.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

This list shows what has been tried so far, on one setup (a Steam Deck with a PS Move ZCM1 and a PS3 Eye). It is a snapshot, not a promise: arcade games differ a lot, and some depend on the TeknoParrot runtime or on your own dump.
RavenGun ships no games. You need your own legally obtained copies.

## Working (47)

These games run on RavenGun's own loader and start straight from RavenGun (double-click), without TeknoParrot; they were played with the lightgun (PS Move or mouse) and checked on the TV. The note says what was tested.

- **Aliens Extermination**: WORKING (2026-10-17, played in mouse mode for 5.5 min: high scores, press start, mission select by shooting, aiming and shooting in the game). Starts by double-click (2026-10-17): PeFillPages (the HASP emulation behind .text that Wine cleared), gamescope with Windowed = 1 at 1920x1080: boot screen, Global VR and PlayMechanix logos, attract with free play / press start. Open: the boot screen reports no GVRIO card and no Aliens guns; input not measured yet.
- **Bug Busters**: WORKING (2026-10-15): double-click in RavenGun, rg-direct with the 32-bit GStreamer from Proton ([Launch] Gst32, docs/gst32.md) for the MPEG-1 videos; without it the game died after MODE SELECT. Played 5.5 min in mouse mode. Runs in a window (taskbar visible).

Coin, START and aiming not measured yet. MOUSE MODE, 2026-10-19 15:05-15:08 (review 16; log direct-MenInBlack-20261019-150532.log, daemon in mouse mode via ravengunctl mouse-gun): coin and START DO arrive, but through the VIRTUAL KEYBOARD (ravengunctl key 5 and key 1), not through the mouse buttons. The 17 October measurement ("coin and START do not arrive" in mouse mode) therefore stands for the MOUSE BUTTONS -- they have no coin or START function -- and was not re-run; what is new today is that the same game does play in mouse mode when coin and START go through the virtual keyboard. ## Playable (3)

These games start from RavenGun and can be played with the lightgun. Some are not yet confirmed with a real PS Move in every detail; the note says what was tested.

- **Gashaaaan Refill!!!!**: Playable after a one-time setup in the test menu (clock, screen, free play; now stored in the game's save data). Then start, aiming and trigger (the ball) work. Test menu: key 0, select with start, execute with P1 aux1.
- **Go Go Strike**: Works: bowling with the Move as trackball (direction and swing set the throw), start (key 1) and trigger (click). 4:3 picture with black bars (gamescope).
- **Luigi's Mansion Arcade**: Starts by double-click in RavenGun (2026-10-14): on our own OpenParrot core and through gamescope the game runs full screen in attract (with the closed core it stopped after ~13 s). Measured earlier: ~6 min of continuous attract/demo on our core (BEWIJS-5MIN.md), with the drop-in rg-pe-hook.dll (see MECHANISME-PE-HOOK.md). NOT playable yet: coin and TEST do not reach the game (DIRECT-ROUTE-INVOER.md).

## Not tested yet (6)

These games are set up, but nobody has tried them with the lightgun yet.

- **Coopers's 9**: Starts by double-click (2026-10-17): with Windowed = 1 under gamescope it shows PLEASE CALIBRATE THE GUN. Calibration and play not measured. Play test 2026-10-17 (mouse mode): 'please calibrate the gun': calibrate in the test menu first.
- **GhostBusters**: UNTESTED with the PS Move: it stays untested until the owner has played it with the Move. Measured on the headless bench on 2026-10-20 with a mouse source and synthetic aim (ravengunctl test-pattern), not with the Move: 3 clean starts straight to attract (FREEPLAY, no gun calibration screen, no money screen: the game's free play setting and both mounted-gun calibrations are seeded from patches/GhostBusters/data into the write layer), "Press ANY BUTTON" (trigger or Start) starts a game, the trigger fires the proton beam and scores, and the game's calibration reticle sits within 7 px of the commanded point at 11 points incl. all four corners (0.1/0.9) and the middle, for both guns, and the beam follows the aim (X and Y both inverted on the RIO channels, see rio-invoer.ini); 6 minutes of play without a crash. Switch ids were read from the game's own Switch Tests screen: Test 3, Service 4, Vol+/- 5/6, coins 0/1/18/2, gun 1 trigger 12/13, gun 2 trigger 15/17; there is no Start, grenade or reload switch, so Cross and reload do nothing. - **House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn**: Measured 2026-10-20 on the shipped no-TeknoParrot route, headless gamescope, started with ravengunctl game start HOTDSD (plain Wine, our own OpenParrot64 core in both exe's, amdaemon.exe first, rg-allsio.dll as the Sega ALLS USB-IO board and the COM1 gun sensor, synthetic platform values, DXVK). Two fixes were needed. (1) rg-rhio.dll answers the board poll 0x25 with a frame whose byte 0 is 0x25 (the game repeats a command until byte 0 of the reply equals the command byte; the old reply 0x94 never ended the loop). MEASURED 2026-10-20 (headless gamescope, plain Wine + [Launch] Dxvk, no wrapper script): rg-rhio.dll now answers the poll command 0x25 with a frame whose byte 0 is 0x25 (BouwAntwoord). A WINEDEBUG trace of the same run shows XAudio2 2.3 (FAudio) working (mastering voice created) but DirectShow failing: 'err:quartz:autoplug Failed to create filter for Wave Parser, hr 0x8007000e' plus seven fixme:ole:CoCreateInstanceEx failures with hr 0x8007000e (E_OUTOFMEMORY); the game itself logs 'Memory: now=3368MB limit=3525MB avail=1016MB' just before, gs2.exe is not large-address-aware, VmPeak of the process 3.8 GB. Working theory (not proven): the 32-bit address space is exhausted at the title scene. rg-amhw.dll: mxsram/SMBus/mxjvs initialise and answer (JVS packets answered, no ERROR 3005). Not reached: attract, coin/Start, trigger. Next step: find what the 32-bit process maps (VmPeak 3.8 GB with a non-LAA exe) and the NULL pointer's origin at 0x5226A0; check whether the missing ./Sound/Sound.lua (file error 2) matters. Earlier notes: MEASURED 2026-10-20 (headless gamescope, plain Wine): with the RingWide recipe of Dream Raiders / Operation G.H.O.S.T. (AmDaemon, [AmDaemon] platformid AAM + gameid SDDV, dropin/rg-amhw.dll, Input jvs + SegaGun2P) the AM library initialises: rg-amhw opens mxsram, the SMBus EEPROM, columba (DMI) and mxsuperio, and gs2.exe talks JVS over the pipe (6 packets, the board answers; ERROR 3005 does not appear any more). With wined3d the game dies with an access violation after 'Failed to get a GL context for adapter' (ERROR 0009 in its dump.dmp), because the headless gamescope Xwayland has no GL; with [Launch] Dxvk = true (user layer, this test only) it creates a fullscreen 1024x768 Direct3D 9 device and then waits. NOT measured: any picture (headless gamescope gives no screenshot for a Wine/DXVK game), so the attract mode is unconfirmed; Status stays parked. Earlier notes: MEASURED 2026-10-19 (item G): the game STARTS and DRAWS on our own loader/core. gs2.exe is 32-bit; it runs through our OpenParrot loader with Core = ravengun in a view (the exe's directory is a real directory, the files are links), Route = tp-shm with Layout = WartranTroopers. The log says "Success! / Loading core... / Resolved target kernel32.dll procedure ... / Have fun :)" and the screenshot (docs/screenshots/tnxk0oc-amilb-error-2026-10-19.png) shows the game's own screen: "ERROR 3005 / AMLIB INITIALZE FAILED" (the game's own typo). So the start, the core and the rendering are fine; the cabinet's AM library (the RingWide I/O) cannot set itself up. What the cabinet itself does (game.bat): first mxGetHwInfo.exe -s mxRingwide.ini and only if that succeeds gs2.exe. That first step is NOT in this profile (there is no PrefixSetup line), because under wine that program goes no further than its own line "mxgethwinfo Ver.1.13 Build:May 18 2012" and exits with status 1 -- it wants the real RingWide hardware. That is why the step is now off and gs2.exe starts directly: which gives this screenshot. Two other things done: the profile name became TNXK0OC (the daemon only allows letters, digits, _ and -, and the folder is named TNXK0O~C; [Identify] Folder still points at the real folder name) and mxRingwide.ini and gs2.ini are real copies in the view so the game does not write to the NAS there. Nothing was written to the NAS: checked with find on the NAS (0 new files) AND in the bwrap writelayer (no new whiteouts, no new files). Next step: find out what AMLIB needs (which files or registers mxGetHwInfo normally fills) and whether that can be imitated.
